cofounderTitle.title: Your co-founder wants a title
cofounderTitle.body: Your co-founder has been introducing themselves as "co-founder and, honestly, sort of CEO". They'd like the paperwork to catch up. Possibly the cap table too.

topUpEquity.label: Top up their equity
topUpEquity.result: Three more points of the company and a hug that went on slightly too long.

coCeo.label: Make you both co-CEOs
coCeo.result: Two CEOs, one company. Margot replied to the announcement with a single question mark.

visionaryTitle.label: Offer "Chief Visionary Officer"
visionaryTitle.result: They accepted the title the way you accept a novelty mug.

sayNo.label: Say titles don't matter yet
sayNo.result: "Easy to say," they said, "for the CEO."

cofounderBurnout.title: Your co-founder is running on empty
cofounderBurnout.body: Your co-founder answered a customer email at 4am, then answered it again at 4:10 with a different answer. Something is going on at home, and something is going on at work.

sabbatical.label: Send them away for a month
sabbatical.result: Out-of-office on, laptop confiscated, plant-watering rota drawn up.
sabbatical.cause: sent your co-founder on a sabbatical

coverForThem.label: Quietly pick up their work
coverForThem.result: You now do two jobs. They noticed, and they won't forget it.

payForTherapy.label: Pay for a proper therapist
payForTherapy.result: The company now has a line item called "wellbeing". It's the best money you've spent.

toughLove.label: Tell them everyone's tired
toughLove.result: You said "we're all tired". They said "right". The conversation was over before it started.
toughLove.cause: told your burnt-out co-founder that everyone was tired

cofounderVision.title: Two visions, one company
cofounderVision.body: Your co-founder has a slide deck about where {{company}} should go. It's good. It's also a different company. They want a decision by Friday.

theirWay.label: Back their vision
theirWay.result: The roadmap swerves. Your co-founder is fizzing with ideas again, most of them expensive.

yourWay.label: Overrule them
yourWay.result: You made the call. They closed their laptop very gently, which was worse than slamming it.

coCeoVote.label: Split the roadmap as co-CEOs
coCeoVote.result: Two roadmaps, one team, and a Venn diagram nobody can read.

partWays.label: Agree it's time to part ways
partWays.result: A long walk, an honest conversation and a lawyer each. They keep the vested shares.

cofounderCovers.title: Your co-founder covered for you
cofounderCovers.body: You slept through the investor call. Your co-founder took it alone, answered every question and told them you were "with a customer". You were with a pillow.

thankPublicly.label: Thank them at stand-up
thankPublicly.result: You told the story against yourself. The team laughed; your co-founder went pink.

returnFavour.label: Take their Monday meetings
returnFavour.result: You sat through their three o'clock. They used the time to actually think.

takeCredit.label: Tell Margot the answers were yours
takeCredit.result: Margot was impressed. Your co-founder heard about it within the week.

giveThemTheRoom.label: Let them lead the next board meeting
giveThemTheRoom.result: They ran the board meeting crisply and finished early. The board has questions about why you don't.

cofounderMeltdown.title: Your co-founder snaps
cofounderMeltdown.body: In the middle of a product review, your co-founder stood up, said "I can't do this any more" and left. Their jacket is still on the chair. So is the team.

apologise.label: Go after them and apologise
apologise.result: You caught them at the bus stop. You said the right things, late, but you said them.

forcedLeave.label: Insist they take real time off
forcedLeave.result: Two weeks, no Slack. Their auto-reply says "back soon" and you choose to believe it.

pointAtValues.label: Point to "We Take Care of Each Other"
pointAtValues.result: Quoting the values doc at them did not land. It is on the wall, though.

letThemGo.label: Accept that they're done
letThemGo.result: They didn't come back for the jacket. You posted it to them with a card.

margotProCeo.title: Margot suggests a grown-up
margotProCeo.body: Margot wants you to meet Graham, who "scaled" a mattress company and is "between things". She says it's just coffee. Graham has already looked at your office.

meetCandidate.label: Have coffee with Graham
meetCandidate.result: Graham called your team "resources" and your product "the asset". The board relaxed.

promiseQuarter.label: Promise her a profitable quarter
promiseQuarter.result: Margot wrote it down. Margot writes everything down.

cofounderVouches.label: Have your co-founder vouch for you
cofounderVouches.result: Your co-founder told Margot that replacing you would be "a ten-year mistake". Graham stays between things.

refuse.label: Tell her you're the CEO
refuse.result: "Of course you are," Margot said, in the past tense somehow.

margotScorecard.title: Margot checks the quarter
margotScorecard.body: Margot has sent a calendar invite titled "The profitable quarter". It has no agenda. It doesn't need one.

showProfit.label: Show her the profit
showProfit.result: Black ink. Margot looked at it for a long time, then forwarded it to her partners with no comment.

showGrowth.label: Show her the growth instead
showGrowth.result: Not profitable, but steep. Margot accepts the substitution, as if at a restaurant.

admitMiss.label: Admit you missed it
admitMiss.result: Margot thanked you for your honesty and made a note that was not about honesty.

redefineQuarter.label: Explain it was a fiscal quarter
redefineQuarter.result: You introduced a fiscal calendar with a quarter of five months. Margot has a finance degree.

margotBridge.title: Margot makes an offer
margotBridge.body: Margot noticed your runway before you mentioned it. She's offering a bridge from Hollowpine, "friendly terms", or some introductions. Both come with Margot.

takeBridge.label: Take the bridge
takeBridge.result: The money arrived before the term sheet did. That's how you know it's friendly.

askForIntros.label: Ask for introductions
askForIntros.result: Margot sent eleven emails with the subject line "you two should meet". Seven replied.

askForCustomers.label: Ask her portfolio to become customers
askForCustomers.result: Three Hollowpine companies signed up the same afternoon. None of them had a choice.

decline.label: Thank her and decline
decline.result: Margot respects a founder who doesn't need her. She'll test it, though.

margotSeat.title: Margot wants a closer look
margotSeat.body: Margot has stopped replying to your updates and started replying to your co-investors. Now she'd like an observer seat "just to stay close".

giveObserver.label: Give her an observer seat
giveObserver.result: Margot observes. Margot takes notes. Board meetings now start on time.

monthlyUpdates.label: Offer detailed monthly updates
monthlyUpdates.result: Your first update is nine pages long. Margot replied "great" to the first line.

lawyerReads.label: Have your lawyer read her the agreement
lawyerReads.result: Your lawyer read clause 14.2 aloud, slowly. The request was withdrawn, coolly.

refuse.label: Politely refuse
refuse.result: Margot said "understood". Her partners will understand it too, at the next board meeting.

margotDownRound.title: Margot orders the house wine
margotDownRound.body: Dinner with Margot. She skips the wine list, asks about "realistic" valuations and mentions a friend's company that "reset expectations" and is "much happier now".
margotDownRound.bluffWorked: Margot believed the other term sheets existed. Your valuation survives the dessert course.
margotDownRound.bluffCalled: Margot asked which funds. You named one. She knows the partner. She called him from the table.

cutBurn.label: Cut costs before she asks
cutBurn.result: The snack budget is gone and so is the second office plant. Margot approves of the plant.

bluff.label: Mention three other term sheets
bluff.result: You said "inbound interest" with a confidence you did not feel.

insiderRound.label: Ask her to lead an insider round
insiderRound.result: Margot said she'd "take it to the partnership", which is Hollowpine for yes.
insiderRound.cause: asked Margot for an insider round

changeSubject.label: Ask about her holiday
changeSubject.result: You learned a great deal about sailing. Margot learned you're avoiding the question.

rivalPanel.title: A panel with Brexton
rivalPanel.body: Upward Summit has put you and Brexton Hale of {{rival}} on the same panel, "Friends or Foes?". The moderator has been told to keep it spicy.

beGracious.label: Be gracious
beGracious.result: You complimented {{rival}}'s design team. Brexton looked confused, then flattered.

roastHim.label: Roast him gently, then not gently
roastHim.result: The clip got a million views. Brexton's reply got two million. Everyone wins except your dignity.

preAnnounce.label: Announce a feature you haven't built
preAnnounce.result: The crowd gasped. Your engineers, watching the stream, also gasped.
preAnnounce.cause: announced an unbuilt feature on stage next to Brexton

agreeWithEverything.label: Agree with everything he says
agreeWithEverything.result: Brexton did most of the talking. The moderator called it "a masterclass in alignment".

rivalPartnership.title: Brexton proposes a truce
rivalPartnership.body: Brexton suggests {{rival}} and {{company}} integrate, "for the ecosystem". It's either a partnership or the opening move of something else, and he's smiling either way.

integrate.label: Build the integration
integrate.result: Users love it. Your engineers and his now share a channel, which is chaos with emoji.

coMarket.label: Run a joint campaign
coMarket.result: A co-branded webinar with both logos the same size, after a week of negotiation about logo size.

lawyerFirst.label: Send the contract to your lawyer
lawyerFirst.result: Your lawyer removed a clause that would have given Brexton your customer list. The rest is fine.

decline.label: Decline politely
decline.result: Brexton said "no hard feelings" and followed three of your engineers on LinkedIn.

rivalFeud.title: Brexton is posting about you
rivalFeud.body: Brexton has posted a thread called "Some companies copy. Some companies create." with a screenshot of your pricing page. {{rival}}'s fans have arrived.
rivalFeud.internWentTooFar: The intern replied to Brexton with a photo of his house. It's been deleted. It has not been forgotten.

fireBack.label: Reply with receipts
fireBack.result: You posted a timeline with dates. The internet brought popcorn and stayed for the sequel.

highRoad.label: Take the high road
highRoad.result: You said "we're focused on our customers". It was boring. It was also correct.

briefDana.label: Give Dana the background
briefDana.result: Dana's piece on "founder feuds" quotes Brexton at length. He comes off badly in his own words.

internAccount.label: Let the intern run the brand account
internAccount.result: The intern has never felt so alive. Your notifications have never been so loud.

rivalFeeler.title: Brexton wants a coffee
rivalFeeler.body: Brexton suggests "a coffee, no agenda" at a café that only does pour-over. His calendar invite is titled "Combining forces?" with the question mark doing a lot of work.

hearHimOut.label: Hear him out
hearHimOut.result: Brexton talked for an hour about synergy. As you left, he said "my people will call your people".
hearHimOut.cause: let Brexton Hale make you an offer over coffee

reverseIt.label: Ask what he'd want for {{rival}}
reverseIt.result: Brexton laughed for slightly too long, then paid for both coffees aggressively.

tipOffDana.label: Let Dana know you're being courted
tipOffDana.result: "{{rival}} circles {{company}}" ran the next morning. Your inbox filled with funds who'd ignored you.

decline.label: Say you're not for sale
decline.result: You said it at the all-hands, too. The team cheered and updated nothing.

rivalOffer.title: {{rival}} makes an offer
rivalOffer.body: Brexton's people called your people, who are you. The offer is real, the premium is modest and the press release has already been drafted with your quote in it.
rivalOffer.walkedAway: Brexton withdrew the offer and announced a "competing initiative" the same day.

sell.label: Sell to Brexton
sell.result: You signed. Brexton posted a photo of the handshake, cropped so he looked taller.

haggle.label: Push for a better price
haggle.result: You asked for thirty percent more and a seat on {{rival}}'s board. Brexton went quiet.

leverage.label: Use it to talk up your next round
leverage.result: Margot heard about the offer from you, first. Your valuation heard about it too.

decline.label: Turn him down
decline.result: You said no. Brexton said "your loss" and started a hiring push the same afternoon.

danaScoop.title: Dana wants a scoop
danaScoop.body: Dana Okafor needs a lead for Thursday's newsletter and thinks {{company}} might be it. She'd like something new, true and preferably both.

realNews.label: Give her real news
realNews.result: A modest, accurate story. Dana thanked you, which journalists rarely do.

embellish.label: Round your numbers up generously
embellish.result: The headline said "explosive growth". Your growth was more of a pop.

aiAngle.label: Pitch the AI feature
aiAngle.result: Dana's editor loved the word "AI" in the headline. Dana loved the demo, which was rarer.

noComment.label: Say there's nothing to share
noComment.result: Dana ran a story about {{rival}} instead. It was very flattering.

danaCorrection.title: Dana checked your numbers
danaCorrection.body: Dana went back to your scoop with a calculator and a former employee. She's drafting a correction and would like to know which of your numbers were real.

admitIt.label: Admit you rounded up
admitIt.result: The correction ran in small type. Dana's trust in you is now also in small type.

doubleDown.label: Stand by every number
doubleDown.result: Dana published your statement next to the spreadsheet. Readers did the maths.

blameCofounder.label: Say your co-founder misspoke
blameCofounder.result: Dana printed the clarification. Your co-founder printed it too, and stuck it to your monitor.

tradeUp.label: Offer her a better, true story
tradeUp.result: Dana traded the correction for a real exclusive. She'll be checking that one, too.

danaFactCheck.title: Dana is fact-checking
danaFactCheck.body: Dana is writing about your category and has a question about your homepage, which says {{company}} is "trusted by teams everywhere". She'd like to know which teams, and where.
danaFactCheck.heldUp: Dana couldn't find anything wrong. Her piece called {{company}} "surprisingly legitimate".
danaFactCheck.fellApart: Dana listed every team that has never heard of you. It was a long list.

fixWebsite.label: Change the homepage today
fixWebsite.result: The homepage now says "trusted by some teams, mostly in one city". Dana noticed the edit.

standByIt.label: Stand by it
standByIt.result: You told her it was "directionally accurate". She asked you to spell "directionally".

sendDashboard.label: Send her the real dashboard
sendDashboard.result: You sent raw numbers, unflattering and true. Dana trusts the numbers and, slightly, you.

lawyerLetter.label: Have your lawyer respond
lawyerLetter.result: A letter about "puffery" on heavy paper. Dana framed it next to the others.

danaHeadsUp.title: Dana gives you a heads-up
danaHeadsUp.body: Dana calls from a personal number. Someone is shopping a story about {{company}} to other outlets, and she thought you'd want to know before it lands somewhere less careful.

getAhead.label: Publish the truth first
getAhead.result: You posted a frank account before the story found a home. It was embarrassing and over by lunch.

giveComment.label: Give her an on-record comment
giveComment.result: Your comment was calm, factual and quoted in full. The other outlets lost interest.

askToSpike.label: Ask her to make it go away
askToSpike.result: "That's not how this works," said Dana, who called as a favour.

lawyerCall.label: Put your lawyer on alert
lawyerCall.result: Your lawyer made two calls and billed for six. The story shrank.

danaHitPiece.title: Dana has written about you
danaHitPiece.body: The Daily Byline ran Dana's piece this morning: "Inside {{company}}: Big Promises, Small Print". It's sourced, it's sharp and it's the top story.
danaHitPiece.visitWentWell: Dana spent a day at {{company}} and left with a follow-up headline: "A Second Look". It was kinder.
danaHitPiece.visitBackfired: Dana spent a day at {{company}} and left with a follow-up headline. Also notes. So many notes.

respondCalmly.label: Respond calmly and correct one fact
respondCalmly.result: You corrected a date and conceded the rest. It was the most adult thing you've done all year.

threadAtMidnight.label: Post a thread at midnight
threadAtMidnight.result: Twenty-three posts, one typo per post. The thread got more coverage than the article.

lawyerUp.label: Send a legal letter
lawyerUp.result: The Byline published your lawyer's letter as a follow-up story.

inviteHerIn.label: Invite her to spend a day here
inviteHerIn.result: Dana accepted, arrived early and brought her own coffee.

vpHeadcountPlan.title: {{name}} has a headcount plan
vpHeadcountPlan.body: {{name}} has sent a hiring plan with a tab for each quarter, a tab for "phase two" and an org chart in which {{name}} is near the top and getting closer.

approveAll.label: Approve the whole plan
approveAll.result: {{name}} is thrilled. The org chart now needs a horizontal scroll.

halveIt.label: Approve one hire
halveIt.result: {{name}} accepted with the smile of someone who will ask again in a month.

routeToPeople.label: Send it through your VP People
routeToPeople.result: Your VP People returned it with forty comments, all of them "why?".

readTheSpreadsheet.label: Read every tab yourself
readTheSpreadsheet.result: Tab nine is a plan to absorb two other departments. You now know who {{name}} really is.

vpOffsite.title: {{name}} wants an offsite
vpOffsite.body: {{name}} says that at their last company, leadership "aligned" at a quarterly offsite in the countryside. They've found a converted barn with a sauna and a facilitator called Rain.

fundOffsite.label: Book the barn
fundOffsite.result: Two days of trust falls and a whiteboard of "north stars". Nobody remembers the stars, but morale is up.

okrsOnly.label: Do OKRs in the office instead
okrsOnly.result: Everyone now has three objectives and nine key results. One of the results is "do OKRs".

pairWithOperator.label: Pair them with your operator
pairWithOperator.result: Your operator turned the offsite agenda into a one-page plan. {{name}} was moved, slightly.

notYet.label: Say "maybe next year"
notYet.result: {{name}} mentioned that their old company had a budget for this. Twice.

turfWar.title: Two VPs, one team
turfWar.body: {{name}} and another VP both believe the growth team reports to them. The growth team has started taking meetings with whoever books first.

backThem.label: Give the team to {{name}}
backThem.result: {{name}} accepted graciously. The other VP accepted by updating their CV.

backTheOther.label: Give it to the other VP
backTheOther.result: {{name}} said "makes sense" and blocked out every Friday afternoon for "strategy".

cofounderRefs.label: Ask your co-founder to referee
cofounderRefs.result: Your co-founder drew a line on a whiteboard and dared anyone to cross it. Nobody did.

operatorDrawsChart.label: Let {{name}} write the ownership doc
operatorDrawsChart.result: {{name}} wrote one page that ended the argument. It's boring, which is how you know it works.

theReorg.title: Time for a reorg
theReorg.body: Nobody is sure who owns onboarding, three teams are building the same settings page and the org chart is a screenshot from last spring. Someone has said the word "reorg".

bigReorg.label: Redraw everything
bigReorg.result: New teams, new managers and a fortnight of people asking where the old Slack channel went.

renameTeams.label: Rename the teams to "squads"
renameTeams.result: Same people, same problems, cooler names. One squad is called "Phoenix". It isn't rising.

vpPeopleRuns.label: Let your VP People run it
vpPeopleRuns.result: A calm, well-explained reorg with one-to-ones for everyone. Suspiciously painless.

leaveIt.label: Leave it alone
leaveIt.result: The three settings pages ship in the same week. They disagree about everything.

regulatorLetter.title: A regulator has written
regulatorLetter.body: The Office of Data Stewardship would like to know where {{company}} keeps its users' data, why, and who said so. The letter is polite. The deadline is not.

hireCompliance.label: Hire a compliance consultancy
hireCompliance.result: The consultants produced a binder, a data map and an invoice. The regulator liked the binder.

lawyerReplies.label: Have your lawyer reply
lawyerReplies.result: Your lawyer's reply was eleven pages and used "notwithstanding" correctly every time.

biggerBanner.label: Make the cookie banner bigger
biggerBanner.result: The banner now covers most of the homepage. Users have learned to click it without reading, as is tradition.
biggerBanner.cause: answered a regulator with a bigger cookie banner

blameTheVendor.label: Blame your analytics vendor
blameTheVendor.result: The vendor's lawyers replied faster than the regulator. Everyone is now copied in on everything.

procurementPortal.title: Procurement has entered the chat
procurementPortal.body: Gristmoor Insurance Group wants to buy {{company}}. First you need to register on their supplier portal, which was built in 2009 and has never been updated, emotionally or otherwise.

fillPortal.label: Spend a week in the portal
fillPortal.result: Forty-one forms, two notarised letters and a fax. The purchase order is real.

signIndemnity.label: Sign their standard contract
signIndemnity.result: You signed on page 38 without reading pages 1 to 37. The money is excellent.
signIndemnity.cause: signed an enterprise contract with unlimited liability

lawyerRedlines.label: Have your lawyer redline it
lawyerRedlines.result: Your lawyer struck out "unlimited" in red ink and a slightly smaller contract came back signed.

walkAway.label: Walk away
walkAway.result: You told Gristmoor you only sell by credit card. They found that charming and baffling.

allHandsMishap.title: The all-hands goes wrong
allHandsMishap.body: You shared your screen to show the roadmap and showed the board deck instead, open on a slide titled "Headcount scenarios". Forty people saw it. Thirty-nine took screenshots.

fullTransparency.label: Walk them through the slide
fullTransparency.result: You explained every scenario, including the bad ones. The questions were hard. The answers were honest.

pivotToVision.label: Move swiftly on to the vision
pivotToVision.result: You talked about the future for twenty minutes. Everyone was thinking about the slide.

quoteTheValues.label: Fall back on the company values
quoteTheValues.result: "We tell each other hard truths," you read. Then you did. It helped.

endEarly.label: Say the Wi-Fi is down and end early
endEarly.result: The Wi-Fi was demonstrably up. Someone was posting about it while you said so.

bigOutage.title: Everything is down
bigOutage.body: {{company}} has been down for three hours. The status page says "investigating", the founder group chat says "lol" and a customer has started counting the minutes publicly.

warRoom.label: Open a war room
warRoom.result: Pizza boxes, a shared doc and a fix at 3am. Uptime is back. Sleep is not.

honestPostmortem.label: Publish an honest post-mortem
honestPostmortem.result: A blameless, detailed write-up. Engineers elsewhere shared it as a good example. Some customers left anyway.

blameProvider.label: Blame your cloud provider
blameProvider.result: The statement said "an upstream issue". The upstream would like a word.
blameProvider.cause: blamed your cloud provider for your own outage

vpEngineeringLeads.label: Let your VP Engineering run it
vpEngineeringLeads.result: Calm incident command, a fix in ninety minutes and a list of things that will never happen again.

firstCustomer.title: Your first paying customer
firstCustomer.body: Someone you've never met has paid for {{company}} with an actual credit card. Their email signature says they run a florist. You have read the receipt nine times.

driveOver.label: Drive over and set it up yourself
driveOver.result: You spent a morning among the lilies. They've told every florist in the county.

frameIt.label: Frame the receipt
frameIt.result: The receipt now hangs above the kettle. Everyone touches the frame for luck.

upsell.label: Upsell them to the annual plan
upsell.result: They took the annual plan. They also took a moment to wonder what they'd signed up for.

caseStudy.label: Ask them for a case study
caseStudy.result: The florist's quote is now on your homepage: "It works, mostly." Conversions went up.

landlordNotices.title: The landlord has noticed
landlordNotices.body: Your landlord has seen four people go into the garage each morning and none of them come out with a car. The lease says "domestic storage". You store a company.
landlordNotices.gotAway: The landlord saw a lot of cardboard boxes and a man reading. He left, satisfied.
landlordNotices.caught: The landlord found the whiteboard behind the boxes. It said "Q3 HIRING". The rent went up.

payExtra.label: Offer him extra rent
payExtra.result: He accepted cash and a promise to stop parking the bins in his space.

offerEquity.label: Offer him a sliver of equity
offerEquity.result: He now owns a tiny bit of {{company}} and asks about "the exit" every time he sees you.

lawyerQuotesLease.label: Have your lawyer quote the lease
lawyerQuotesLease.result: Your lawyer found the clause allowing "home office use". The landlord found it too, sadly.

hideTheWhiteboard.label: Hide everything before he visits
hideTheWhiteboard.result: You turned the garage into a garage in forty minutes. It looked staged, because it was.

friendInvests.title: A friend wants in
friendInvests.body: Your university flatmate has done well in insurance and wants to invest twenty-five thousand dollars. They say they believe in you. They also say "ten-bagger" without irony.

takeIt.label: Take the money on a handshake
takeIt.result: The money arrived with a text: "Don't lose it lol". The "lol" is doing a lot.
takeIt.cause: took twenty-five thousand dollars from a friend on a handshake

properPaperwork.label: Do it properly, with paperwork
properPaperwork.result: Your lawyer wrote it up properly. Your friend has never felt so legally loved.

smallerCheque.label: Take a smaller cheque
smallerCheque.result: Five thousand dollars, low stakes and no awkward weddings. Probably.

keepTheFriend.label: Say no to protect the friendship
keepTheFriend.result: They were relieved, then offended, then relieved again. You bought the next round.

parentsWorried.title: Your parents have questions
parentsWorried.body: Your parents rang to ask, gently, whether {{company}} is "a real job yet". Your mother has printed out an advert for an accountancy graduate scheme.

explainSaas.label: Explain the business model to them
explainSaas.result: Two hours on recurring revenue. Your dad now says "churn" at dinner parties.

promiseDeadline.label: Promise a real job if it fails
promiseDeadline.result: You named a date. Your mother wrote it on the calendar in pen.
promiseDeadline.cause: promised your parents you'd get a real job if this didn't work out

acceptCheque.label: Accept the cheque they offer
acceptCheque.result: Ten thousand dollars and the words "we're not investors, we're your parents".

friendVouches.label: Have your investor friend reassure them
friendVouches.result: Your flatmate told your parents it was "a ten-bagger". They sent another five thousand anyway.

hackathonPrize.title: You won a hackathon
hackathonPrize.body: You entered a weekend hackathon for the free pizza and accidentally won it. The prize is ten thousand dollars and a cardboard cheque too big for the car.

takeTheCash.label: Take the cash
takeTheCash.result: The cardboard cheque is now your office door. The real one cleared on Tuesday.

recruitRunnersUp.label: Recruit the runners-up
recruitRunnersUp.result: Two engineers who built a working app in 48 hours on energy drinks. They're available.

pitchTheJudges.label: Pitch the judges
pitchTheJudges.result: One judge was a Hollowpine associate. She's mentioned you to Margot, favourably.

demoTheAi.label: Demo the AI feature
demoTheAi.result: The judges awarded you the main prize and a special prize for "use of AI". Two cheques.

domainSquatter.title: Someone owns your domain
domainSquatter.body: The .com for {{company}} belongs to a man called Desmond who registered it in 2003 "just in case". He'll part with it for fifteen thousand dollars and a story.
domainSquatter.handedOver: Desmond read the letter, sighed and transferred the domain. He sent a short poem about it.
domainSquatter.priceDoubled: Desmond read the letter and doubled the price. He's framed the letter.

payHim.label: Pay Desmond
payHim.result: The domain is yours. Desmond told you the story. It was mostly about 2003.

settleForPrefix.label: Use "get{{company}}" instead
settleForPrefix.result: You're now get{{company}}.com. Half your users keep typing the other one.
settleForPrefix.cause: settled for a domain with "get" in front

lawyerLetter.label: Have your lawyer write to him
lawyerLetter.result: A stern, trademark-heavy letter is on its way to Desmond's mailbox.

dropTheVowels.label: Drop the vowels from your name
dropTheVowels.result: The new domain was available and looks like a sneeze. Investors think it's very on-trend.

cofounderReturns.feed: Your co-founder is back from their break: tanned, rested and full of opinions about the Slack channels.
